name: GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin)
lead: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide that stimulates growth hormone (GH) release by acting on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor. It belongs to the family of growth hormone-releasing peptides developed from work led by Cyril Bowers at Tulane University and by Polygen in Germany. [1][2]

Medically, GHRP-2 is used in Japan as a diagnostic stimulation test for adult growth hormone deficiency. [3][4] Outside that test it is not an approved treatment. In bodybuilding and peptide communities it is used as a GH secretagogue, commonly alongside a GHRH analogue such as sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29), for muscle, recovery and body composition. [5][6][7]

Human studies establish that it releases GH, but no clinical trial cited here shows that it improves muscle or appearance in healthy people. A 2020 review of GH secretagogues in hypogonadal men notes that clinical efficacy data remain largely lacking. [8]
infobox: Polygen (Germany) and Tulane University (US), per Drugs in R&D
Intravenous, subcutaneous, oral and intranasal forms have been studied

paras: In Japan the GHRP-2 test is recommended as a convenient and safe GH stimulation test for adult GH deficiency, with a peak GH cut-off used to define severe deficiency. [3][4] Prescribing information of that kind concerns diagnosis, not body-composition treatment.

Research has also tested GHRP-2 infusions in prolonged critical illness, in some studies combined with TRH, in which the aim was to reactivate pituitary hormone release and improve metabolic status. [9][10]

Human trials have focused on endocrine responses and diagnostics rather than appearance. A review of the GHRP class reports that GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and hexarelin potently stimulate GH release in animals and humans, and that the mechanism remains partly unclear. [1][11] A randomised trial in seven young men reported evidence against a role for the GHRP axis in human slow-wave sleep regulation. [12]

Studies in critically ill patients found that continuous GHRP-2 infusion, particularly combined with TRH, reactivated pituitary hormone release and gave limited metabolic benefit over several days. [9][10] A forum post discusses a 2014 Japanese trial in prepubertal children with GH deficiency examining whether GHRP-2 improved growth, and argues from it that the peptide is unlikely to help height. [13] That reading is the poster's own and the trial is not independently reviewed here.
No studies found of GHRP-2 for muscle gain or fat loss in healthy people.

GHRP-2 acts as an agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, the receptor for ghrelin, in the pituitary and hypothalamus, and has no structural similarity to GHRH. [1][2][14] Reviews suggest it may counter somatostatin and partly act through GHRH-mediated mechanisms. [1]

In animals, GHRP-2 has also raised food intake and fat mass. In mice lacking NPY it increased body weight and fat mass, and in neonatal chicks ghrelin and GHRP-2 inhibited food intake. [15][16] A 2005 study found anti-inflammatory effects in arthritic rats. [17]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: On T Nation, GHRP-2 appears in peptide logs next to testosterone cycles and in pairings with sermorelin or modified GRF (1-29). [5][6][7][18] One user says GHRP-6 makes many people eat heavily, which is why they chose GHRP-2. [19]
On looksmax.org one thread argues GHRP-2 is probably ineffective for height growth; a reply attributes this to its acting through the ghrelin pathway. [13]

Controlled safety data for healthy people using it for cosmetic goals are not available in the sources used here. In animals GHRP-2 raised appetite and fat mass. [15] Reviews of GH secretagogues also note the lack of long-term efficacy and safety data. [8]

timeline.event: Cyril Bowers' group at Tulane University begins synthesising small GH-releasing peptides, the class from which GHRP-2 emerged. [14]
A European Journal of Endocrinology review describes GHRP-2 as available for human study. [1]
Pralmorelin is profiled in Drugs in R&D as an orally active GH-releasing peptide used as a GH deficiency diagnostic. [2]

lore.intro: GHRP-2 is discussed on T Nation as a GH secretagogue stacked with GHRH analogues, and on looksmax.org in a thread about whether it can influence height. [5][6][13]

claims.claim: GHRP-2 raises GH, helping muscle growth and recovery
claims.believers: Users report taking it with testosterone cycles and say GH-releasing peptides produce gains without water retention. [5][7][20]
claims.experts: Trials confirm GH release, but a review states clinical efficacy data for body composition remain largely lacking. [1][8]

claims.believers: Some forum users ask whether GH secretagogues could add height.
claims.experts: A forum post cites a 2014 Japanese paediatric study to argue against height benefit, and a reply says the ghrelin pathway is not expected to help. [13]

claims.believers: One user reports improved sleep quality after a couple of months of use. [6]
claims.experts: A randomised trial in healthy men found evidence against a role for the GHRP axis in slow-wave sleep. [12]

claims.claim: GHRP-2 is preferable to GHRP-6 because it causes less hunger
claims.believers: Users say GHRP-6 makes people eat everything in sight, while GHRP-2 was chosen for that reason, though one still reports overeating. [19]
claims.experts: Animal studies show GHRP-2 raising food intake and fat mass, so appetite effects are documented. [15]

claims.claim: GHRP plus GHRH produces synergistic GH release
claims.believers: Forum posts state that GHRH combined with GHRP-6, GHRP-2 or hexarelin synergistically releases GH. [7][18]
claims.experts: Reviews describe distinct receptors for GHRP and GHRH; no cited trial examines the combination for appearance. [1]

card.summary: A potent ghrelin-receptor GH-releasing peptide: a real diagnostic in Japan, but nothing shows it builds muscle in healthy users.
card.note: Raises appetite and GH; no trials for appearance goals.

quick.overview:
GHRP-2 is a lab-made peptide that mimics ghrelin to trigger growth hormone release. It is used in Japan to test for GH deficiency, and in forums it is stacked with GHRH analogues for muscle and recovery.

Trials prove it raises GH, but none cited show better muscle or looks in healthy people.
quick.mechanism: It binds the ghrelin (GH secretagogue) receptor in the pituitary and hypothalamus, driving GH release through a path separate from GHRH.
quick.risks: Appetite and fat mass increases appear in animal studies, and long-term safety data for cosmetic use are lacking. It is not approved for body-composition use.
